proposed_change.summary: Create a new feature profile on object sdk covering the buyer-facing image upload flow, visitor identification, and the AI-effect-gated upload rate limit. None of this exists in canonical context today.
proposed_change.rationale: TIB-5460 is the first task to touch this area and canonical context cannot support it at all. The retriever's full-text scan of all 9 objects returned: 'visitor' 0 hits, 'quota' 0, 'throttle' 0, 'upload limit' 0, 'AI effect' 0, 'remove background' 0, 'device info' 0, 'incognito' 0. The word 'upload' does not occur once in sdk/features/storefront-buyer-facing/profile.json and 0 of its 38 published checks involve an upload. The gap is not even listed among that KB's 21 declared coverage_gaps, i.e. it is unrecognised rather than merely open.
capabilities_to_model: Buyer selects an image for an artwork field on the storefront product page and it is uploaded.
Visitor identity: signed thumbmark fetched from GET /merchant/{platform}/thumbmark, cached in localStorage key teeinblue_signed_thumbmark with no expiry.
Fallback identity when the signed thumbmark is unavailable at upload time (the subject of TIB-5460).
Upload rate limit keyed per visitor + per product + per window; default 5 per window; window 1h production / 5min staging.
Gating rule: only uploads using an AI effect (Remove Background, AI Enhance / Image Filter, Text-to-Image) are limited; a plain upload is never limited.
Buyer-facing error state at the limit ('Upload limit exceeded').
proposed_change.knowledge_kind_guidance: Everything above must be recorded as CONFIRMED_EXPECTED only where a Jira statement supports it AND that statement is confirmed as dev-authored (see the open question on comment authorship). Anything derived from observing staging is OBSERVED_CURRENT. The constants (5 per window, 8s, 1 retry) come from Jira comment 51220 only and have never been observed.
proposed_change.explicitly_not_proposed: No expected-result text is proposed here. This KCP asks for the area to be modelled, not for TIB-5460's claims to be adopted as canon. Modelling should follow a real Flow 1 exploration.
